# flashalpha-historical-examples

> 21 backtest essays for options strategies on QuantConnect LEAN.
> Side-by-side C# and Python. Powered by flashalpha-quantconnect.

## Data provenance

Every FlashAlpha API response carries `data_as_of`: when each upstream feed last delivered
to the node that answered - equity and index spot, their option chains, futures and futures
options, the classified trade tape, settled open interest, and the macro series, each
reported separately because they arrive over different pipes and fail independently. `null`
means that node has not seen that feed, not that it is broken. Read each feed against its
own cadence: settled open interest dated to the previous session's close is correct, while
an options feed an hour behind during the regular session is not. `endpoint_version`
identifies the deployment. Full reference:
https://flashalpha.com/docs/lab-api-overview#response-envelope

## Essays — Dealer positioning
- [Gamma scalping in QuantConnect](essays/a-dealer-positioning/01-gamma-scalping/README.md): Backtest a long-SPY drift trade gated by FlashAlpha's dealer-gamma regime label — long when dealers are net long gamma (low-vol drift), flat when they're net short gamma (vol expansion).
- [GEX regime following](essays/a-dealer-positioning/02-gex-regime-following/README.md): Hold SPY when dealer NetGex trends up week-over-week and rotate to cash on negative-gamma rolls — a momentum spin on the regime gate from the gamma-scalping flagship.
- [Gamma flip strike trading](essays/a-dealer-positioning/03-gamma-flip-strike/README.md): Pin the gamma-flip strike (where NetGex crosses zero) as a dynamic support/resistance level; trade pullbacks toward it inside positive-gamma regimes.
- [Negative-gamma vol expansion play](essays/a-dealer-positioning/04-negative-gamma-vol-expansion/README.md): Buy a long-vol structure (straddle proxy via VXX) on the first day NetGex flips negative — explicitly trade the vol-expansion regime that the gamma-scalping flagship sits out.
- [Pin-risk avoidance (0DTE)](essays/a-dealer-positioning/05-pin-risk-avoidance-0dte/README.md): Skip SPY 0DTE option entries when ExposureSummary shows the underlier within 0.5σ of a high-OI strike — measure how often 'pin risk' actually pins.

## Essays — Vanna / charm / VEX
- [Charm-flow afternoon timing](essays/b-vanna-charm-vex/06-charm-flow-afternoon/README.md): Time intraday SPY entries to the afternoon charm-flow window (last 90 minutes) using the dealer-charm column of ChexBar — when dealers must rebalance into close, the drift edge concentrates.
- [Vanna-shock reversal](essays/b-vanna-charm-vex/07-vanna-shock-reversal/README.md): Fade SPY single-day moves > 1.5σ when VexBar's net vanna spiked the day prior — vanna shocks tend to mean-revert as dealers re-hedge volatility-of-volatility exposure.
- [Combined-greek regime grid](essays/b-vanna-charm-vex/08-combined-greek-regime-grid/README.md): Build a 4-quadrant regime grid from the sign of NetGex × the sign of NetVex (gamma + vanna) and run a directional SPY trade in only the long-gamma-positive-vanna cell.

## Essays — VRP / volatility
- [VRP harvest short-vol](essays/c-vrp-volatility/09-vrp-harvest-short-vol/README.md): Sell a delta-hedged 30-day SPY straddle when VrpBar's 60-day variance-risk-premium z-score is positive — classical short-vol carry, gated on the empirical VRP rather than on flat IV-rank.
- [IV-rank entry filter](essays/c-vrp-volatility/10-iv-rank-entry-filter/README.md): Use VolatilityBar's IV-rank as a second gate on top of any directional signal — only enter SPY longs when IV-rank is in its bottom quintile, so you're not paying for vol that's already priced.
- [Realized vs implied divergence](essays/c-vrp-volatility/11-realized-vs-implied-divergence/README.md): Compare AdvVolatilityBar's realized vol (Parkinson estimator) against its IV surface; when realized exceeds implied by > 4 vol points for 5 sessions, fade SPY's directional bias.
- [Vol term-structure spread](essays/c-vrp-volatility/12-vol-term-structure-spread/README.md): Long the 60-day - 30-day implied-vol spread via VolatilityBar — capture the term-structure mean-reversion that emerges after vol-curve inversions.

## Essays — 0DTE
- [0DTE Friday gamma squeeze](essays/d-zero-dte/13-friday-gamma-squeeze/README.md): On 0DTE Friday, take a long-SPY position if NetGex > $2B at the open — Friday-only exposure to the dealer-pinning lift that compounds across the morning.
- [0DTE pin gravitation](essays/d-zero-dte/14-pin-gravitation/README.md): Trade SPY mean-reversion toward MaxPainBar's max-pain strike during the last hour of 0DTE expiration days; measure how often max-pain actually pins.
- [0DTE intraday gamma flip](essays/d-zero-dte/15-intraday-gamma-flip/README.md): Use hourly GEX snapshots to detect NetGex sign changes inside the trading session, and rebalance SPY exposure on the flip — intraday version of the gamma-scalping flagship.
- [0DTE expected-move straddle](essays/d-zero-dte/16-expected-move-straddle/README.md): Buy a 0DTE straddle when ZeroDteBar's expected-move band is < 0.6× realized vol — explicit vol mispricing trade on options expiring same-day.

## Essays — Cross-signal / multi-asset
- [Dispersion: SPY vs RTY](essays/e-cross-signal/17-dispersion-spy-vs-rty/README.md): Long IWM, short SPY (vol-weighted) when SurfaceBar's IV-skew differential between SPY and IWM exceeds 1.5σ — index dispersion trade gated on the relative skew, not on simple correlation.
- [Calendar carry on positive-gamma days](essays/e-cross-signal/18-calendar-carry-positive-gamma/README.md): Sell a short-dated, buy a long-dated SPY ATM call (calendar spread) on days when NetGex is positive and the term structure is in contango — collect both theta and carry only in the favorable regime.
- [Max-pain reversion](essays/e-cross-signal/19-max-pain-reversion/README.md): Trade SPY toward MaxPainBar's strike whenever spot is > 2% away from it, with a stop at the gamma-flip — explicit pin-reversion trade outside expiration weeks.
- [Earnings vol contraction](essays/e-cross-signal/20-earnings-vol-contraction/README.md): Sell single-name implied vol the morning after earnings when AdvVolatilityBar shows IV > 30% above its trailing 30-day average — the classic post-earnings vol-crush trade, gated on the size of the pre-print premium.
